name: Tolstraat 160 (Cinétol, Tempel)
description: A concrete hall built for the Theosophical Society in the Netherlands to a design by Brinkman and Van der Vlugt, the architects of the Van Nelle factory, in the Nieuwe Zakelijkheid style. Its plan is a quarter circle under a kind of tent roof, with a closed ground floor and an open upper storey behind a gallery that runs all the way round. Later it was the Cinétol cinema and a branch of the public library; since 2022 it has been Tempel Amsterdam, with workspaces for the cultural sector, and since 2024 it has also housed De Appel, a centre for contemporary art.
funFact: To keep columns out of the quarter-circle meeting hall, special concrete roof trusses had to be designed. The grey concrete was later rendered over, which gives the building its bright look today.
